table3_1_validity.title: Table 3.1 Cluster validity of the selected partition (c* = 2) against 1,000 permutation nulls
table3_1_validity.note: One-sided permutation p-values. The selection-aware row compares the best value over c = 2–8 with the best value attained on each null dataset, as in Table 3.5. The null selected c* = 2 in 86% of replicates.

table3_2_replication.title: Table 3.2 Stability and replication of the subgroups
table3_2_replication.note: Stability: 200 subsamples of 80% of the participants. Replication: means over 50 random splits of each participant's conversations into halves A and B; subgroups formed on half A; significance by Kruskal–Wallis tests with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment over 21 models. Reliability: null mean [95% range].

table3_3_baselines.title: Table 3.3 Algorithm 1 and other clustering methods at c = 2, each against its own permutation null
table3_3_baselines.note: Silhouettes are computed on the same P-HFE profiles; 100 null replicates per method.

table3_4_external.title: Table 3.4 Sociodemographic validation of the subgroups
table3_4_external.note: Attributes were not used for clustering. Cramér's V: association with subgroup membership; R²: share of the variation in preference profiles explained by the attribute (PERMANOVA). 999 permutations each.

table3_5_sensitivity.title: Table 3.5 Sensitivity to the balancing parameters and robustness checks
table3_5_sensitivity.note: Each configuration was compared with the same 1,000 permutation nulls as Table 3.1; the graded encoding with 200.

tableA1_representation.title: Table A1 Representation of sociodemographic groups by the pooled and the SCO-FCM consensus rankings
tableA1_representation.note: Kendall's τ between a group's model ranking and the ranking named in the column; p tests whether the group is represented worse than a random group of the same size (999 permutations).
